rationale_evidence.anchor: 25N (094210) -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra. FIRST PRINCIPLE (section25N.1): "evidence is not a scalar". SIX SEPARATE CONCEPTS: Support, Reliability, Authority, Probability, Confidence, Independence. ... IMPOSSIBILITY-STYLE RESULT ... Evidence has no intrinsic universal weight
rationale_evidence.statement: Step 25H (092308) formalizes a governed Sarathi decision operator S(K,G,D,M,C) -> DecisionResult in {Decision, HumanDecisionRequired, InsufficientKnowledge, GovernanceBlocked, ModelUnderspecified}, with probability treated as optional (decisions may rest on constraints/dominance alone) and three decision modes (deterministic/model-based/human-escalation). Step 25N (094210) states as a first principle that evidence is not a scalar, decomposing it into six separate concepts (Support, Reliability, Authority, Probability, Confidence, Independence), gives the likelihood-ratio combination law LR(E1..En)=product of LR(Ei) under conditional independence while flagging independence as an assumption never to be auto-applied, distinguishes a Statistical aggregation regime from a Qualitative one that must never be silently mixed, and derives by counter-scenario (high-authority/low-reliability versus low-authority/high-reliability evidence) an impossibility-style result that evidence aggregation is domain/model dependent, boxed as 'Evidence has no intrinsic universal weight' with effect instead modeled as a relation Effect(E,A|C,M).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Step 26 (101406) ... KEY DERIVATION (section26.5): epistemic Zero arises from observational equivalence -- Zero is given an information-theoretic ground ... section26.7 "identifiability is more important than confidence".
rationale_evidence.statement: Step 26 grounds epistemic Zero in observational equivalence (two world states that produce the same observation are indistinguishable in principle, not merely unmeasured), argues identifiability matters more than confidence, defines observational equivalence, identifiability, model validity region, domain of applicability, an abstraction function with leakage, an observability matrix, and an instrumentation gap; distinguishes safe sensing from world-changing action; and derives six boxed inequalities (Model!=Reality, Observation!=State, Computability!=Justifiability, Confidence!=Identifiability, Correlation!=Causation, and that Unknown does not mean the system should guess), giving the system a way to state 'I cannot know this from the currently available observations' as distinct from ordinary uncertainty.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Step 29 (101614) ... section29.24 the architectural discipline: "do we need an SMT solver everywhere? No" ... section29.31 "constraint confidence is unnecessary" ... section29.67 (the honest gap): "an internally consistent knowledge base can still be completely wrong"
rationale_evidence.statement: Step 29 formalizes satisfiability (SAT(K and C) -> SAT/UNSAT) and satisfiability-modulo-theories for constraints like Version bounds, states the architectural discipline that solvers should be used only where complexity justifies them (not universally), catalogues eight constraint classes (Structural, Temporal, Semantic, Cardinality, Authorization, Safety, Statistical, Causal), argues constraints are typed, not probabilistic ('constraint confidence is unnecessary'), introduces a consistency vector generalizing a single consistency score plus unit/dimensional-analysis consistency (judged genuinely novel in the corpus), and prefers a Generate->Verify->Accept pipeline over Generate->Trust. Ends with an honest, load-bearing admission (section 29.67) that an internally consistent knowledge base can still be completely wrong (InternallyConsistent and ExternallyIncorrect can co-occur), explicitly handed off to step 30.
